full_judgment: 7. With regard to his first submission that impugned judgment is not a proper judgment of reversal, Mr. Islam submitted that the appellate Court ought to have said something about the genuineness or otherwise of the two documents, namely, Amalnama Ext. 1 and Kabuliat Ext. 2. In this connection he has referred to the decision of Khondker Mohiuddin Vs. Syed Moin Ahmed, reported in 28 DLR(AD) at page 85 which has been also been relied only the learned Advocate for the opposite party. It is true that these tow documents were not dissected by the lower appellate court, but the fact remains that the decision of the trial Court is not solely based on these two documents. The main consideration which weighed upon the mind of the trial Court is that the plaintiff failed to prove that he was in possession of the suit land at any time within 12 years next before the filing of the suit and as such the Court found the suit to be barred by limitation. In this view of the matter, I find that non-discussion of the two documents, namely, Amalnama and Kabuliyat has not caused any miscarriage of justice.
